newsitem.title: BELGIUM: SOCCER-BRUGES' SPEHAR CLOSE TO MONACO TRANSFER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BRUGES' SPEHAR CLOSE TO MONACO TRANSFER.

text.p: Croat striker Robert Spehar is expected to move to Monaco from Club Bruges on Thursday, his Belgian club said.
"I expect it to be finalised today... and it's more likely that he'll leave than that he'll stay," Club Bruges secretary general Jacques De Nolf told Reuters on Thursday.

De Nolf, who declined to comment on media reports that Monaco were offering 200 million Belgian francs ($5.26 million) for Spehar, said Monaco wanted to sign the Croat before August 15 to be able to field him in their Champions' League games.
If they wait longer Spehar can only play in the Champions' League from 1998, he said.
Monaco wanted Spehar, last year's top scorer in the Belgian first division, to replace Brazil's Sonny Anderson who has left for Barcelona.
Spehar, 27, told Belgian television: "Monaco are really serious about buying me and I must say that I'm really interested and also want to go there."
"When I was little I dreamed about playing for a big club like Monaco...also it was my dream to play in the Champions' League," Spehar said.
Spehar and Bruges announced last week the Croat had extended his contract, which expired at the end of this season, until 2000 at sharply improved terms.
But Spehar said he had reached a deal with Bruges but had not actually signed the contract.
"I didn't sign my contract (with Bruges) and I will not sign the contract," said Spehar, who has scored 41 goals in 50 matches since joining Club Bruges before the 1995-1996 season.
He scored a hat-trick in Bruges' first match of the new league championship on Saturday.
Spehar did not play for Bruges in their UEFA Cup second preliminary round match against Slovenians HIT Gorica on Tuesday, claiming he had a slight thigh injury.
But Belgian media suggested Spehar's injury might have been diplomatic and linked to his expected transfer to Monaco.
